authoredPrompt: This figure is a three-dimensional vector field plot drawn inside a light blue wireframe cube, with black x, y, and z axes running through it; x points toward the lower left, y to the right, and z vertically. A small shaded blue sphere sits where the axes cross, marked with the label 0, standing for a large mass at the origin. Arrows fill the interior of the cube and every one points inward toward that sphere. Those closest to the origin are long and bright orange, those at intermediate distance shorter and teal, and those near the corners and faces reduced to small dashes, so length and color together carry the magnitude of the field. Several of the longest arrows lie along the axis directions and meet the sphere head on. Because length and direction vary independently, the reader takes in both at once: the field aims at the central mass everywhere, and its strength climbs sharply as distance to the origin shrinks. The plot renders the gravitational field of a point mass, making visible the uniformly attractive radial direction and the rapid growth in magnitude near the source.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for distance from the central mass: the learner drags a sample point radially outward or inward and its vector changes length and color, making clear that the field always points toward the origin while magnitude grows sharply as r decreases.
- Toggle between direction-only and magnitude-colored views: the learner switches from equal-length inward arrows to the full scaled field, making clear the distinction between attractive radial direction and inverse-distance strength.
authoredContext:
The figure shows what this gravitational field looks like for a large mass at the origin. Note that the magnitudes of the vectors increase as the vectors get closer to the origin.

A visual representation of gravitational vector field F=−Gm1m2〈xr3,yr3,zr3〉 for a large mass at the origin.

A visual representation of the given gravitational vector field in three dimensions. The magnitudes of the vectors increase as the vectors get closer to the origin. The arrows point in, towards the mass at the origin.

evaluation.notes: Faithful reproduction of the attractive inverse-square vector field with correct inward-pointing arrows, orange-to-teal color gradient, wireframe cube, and labeled axes; interactive slider and direction-only toggle add pedagogical value without distorting the figure.
